# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1071

## Korean source

```text
  1|1071화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|
  6|나는 신속하고 주위의 상황을 읽고 판단했다.
  7|
  8|그리고 그중에서도 최우선으로 둔 것은, 사방에서 몰려오는 먼지구름의 크기와 지면으로부터 전해지는 진동의 세기를 통하여 적들의 숫자를 가늠하는 것이었다.
  9|
 10|‘최소 일만. 절대 그 이하는 아니야.’
 11|
 12|당연하게도 상황은 좋지 않았다.
 13|
 14|어림짐작하기에도 무려 아군의 세 배가 넘는 머릿수.
 15|
 16|더불어 지금 이 순간에도 시시각각 가까워지는 적들은 지치지도, 쉽게 죽지도 않는 괴물들이니까.
 17|
 18|‘심지어 그중에는 저놈 같은 또 다른 변이체도 있겠지.’
 19|
 20|나는 고개를 돌려 바라보았다.
 21|
 22|머리가 절반으로 쪼개진 채, 완전한 죽음을 맞이한 거인의 시체를.
 23|
 24|장담컨대 저 거대한 체구를 지닌 괴물의 정체는 트롤도, 오우거도 아니다.
 25|
 26|21세기 현대를 혼돈의 구렁텅이로 빠트린 대격변 이후, 지금까지 나타난 모든 종류의 괴물이 기록된 몬스터 백과사전에도 저런 괴물은 없다.
 27|
 28|앞서 내가 마음속으로 읊조렸던 것처럼, 그야말로 변이체(變異體)라는 표현이 어울리는 존재였다.
 29|
 30|어느 순간부터 무림에서 모습을 드러냈던, 또 다른 괴물들처럼.
 31|
 32|‘그래, 그때와 같은 흐름이다.’
 33|
 34|변이체의 등장은 이번이 처음이 아니다.
 35|
 36|호북에서도, 남만야수궁에서도 이와 비슷한 일들이 벌어졌었다.
 37|
 38|그리고 언제나 그 모든 것의 중심에는, 천주(天主)를 따르는 추종자들과 그들이 불러온 ‘균열’이 있었음을 나는 똑똑히 기억하고 있다.
 39|
 40|‘그렇다는 건, 설마…….’
 41|
 42|문득 뇌리를 스치는 한 줄기의 불길한 생각.
 43|
 44|그러나 나는 이내 고개를 내저어 상념을 끊어 냈다.
 45|
 46|설령 조금 전 떠오른 생각이 전부 사실이라 해도, 지금은 당장 눈앞의 적들을 쓰러트리는 것이 우선이었으니까.
 47|
 48|“사마표, 정호군.”
 49|
 50|불쑥 입을 연 나는 두 사람을 똑바로 응시하며 말을 이었다.
 51|
 52|“지금부터 각각 좌, 우를 맡는다.”
 53|
 54|말없이 고개를 숙인 사마표와 정호군이 즉각 움직였다.
 55|
 56|각각 일천의 수하를 거느린 저들은 지금부터 아군의 양 날개가 되어 줄 것이다.
 57|
 58|이 긴박한 상황에서 시간을 지체시킨 웬수 덩어리인 동시에, 한편으로는 기가 막힌 우연의 일치로 적들을 맞이할 준비 시간을 벌어 주었던 어느 초절정 고수와 함께.
 59|
 60|“대인.”
 61|
 62|“응? 나? 나는 빠지면 안 되나? 저들과는 별 악감정도 없는데.”
 63|
 64|“시발 대인아.”
 65|
 66|“……어디로 가면 되겠나?”
 67|
 68|“좌우측. 번갈아 가면서 위급한 쪽을 도와주십시오.”
 69|
 70|“끄응. 알겠네.”
 71|
 72|이로써 아군의 양 날개는 더욱더 날카롭고 튼튼해질 것이다.
 73|
 74|정신이 오락가락하긴 해도, 초절정 고수가 버티고 있는 한 결코 쉽게 허물어질 수 없을 테니까.
 75|
 76|“빈도는 어찌하면 되겠는가?”
 77|
 78|공동파의 장문인, 현천진인의 물음에 나는 즉각 답했다.
 79|
 80|“장문인께서는 공동파의 제자들과 함께 후미를 맡아 주십시오.”
 81|
 82|“종남파에게 선봉을 빼앗긴 것은 아쉽지만, 지금 같은 상황에서는 본문이 가장 중요한 역할을 맡아야겠지. 도우의 뜻은 잘 알겠네.”
 83|
 84|적들에 의한 포위망이 어느 정도 갖추어진 상황에서는 선봉보다도 후미가 중요한 법.
 85|
 86|그런 의미에서 보자면 현천진인은 평범한 무림인과는 달리 전술에 대한 이해도가 있는 사람이었다.
 87|
 88|정마대전이라는 거대한 전란을 온몸으로 헤쳐나온 노강호였고, 그렇기에 내 의도를 어렵지 않게 알아차린 것이다.
 89|
 90|물론, 그런 현천진인조차도 모든 것을 꿰뚫어 본 것은 아니었지만.
 91|
 92|“선봉은 종남이 아닙니다.”
 93|
 94|“그게 무슨.”
 95|
 96|순간 의아해하는 현천진인을 뒤로한 채, 나는 긴장된 얼굴로 검을 쥐고 있던 한 사람을 불렀다.
 97|
 98|“혁소평. 너와 종남파 또한 공동파를 도와 후미를 맡는다.”
 99|
100|종남일룡(終南一龍) 혁소평.
101|
102|대설산에서의 전투로 중상을 입은 탓에 감숙에 남을 수밖에 없었던 풍운검군 대신, 살아남은 종남파의 제자들을 이끌고 있던 그가 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
103|
104|아니, 비단 혁소평 한 사람뿐만이 아니라 내 한 마디 한 마디에 촉각을 곤두세우고 있던 주변인들 모두가 동시에 보인 반응이기도 했다.
105|
106|“그렇다면 선봉은…….”
107|
108|혁소평이 말꼬리를 흐린 그때, 누군가의 걸걸한 목소리가 모두의 귓가를 파고들었다.
109|
110|“뭐 하고 자빠졌느냐. 냉큼 후미로 빠지지 않고.”
111|
112|화왕(火王) 적천강.
113|
114|바로 그였다.
115|
116|그리고 이 드넓은 무림에 자신의 발자국을 난폭하게 박아 넣은 거인의 옆자리에는, 왕을 넘어 별이라 불리게 된 한 여인이 있었다.
117|
118|철컥.
119|
120|말없이 두 자루의 곡도를 연결하여 거대한 활을 완성시키는 궁성(弓星)의 모습에 모두가 입을 다물었다.
121|
122|저들이 누구인가.
123|
124|화왕과 궁성이다.
125|
126|가장 난폭한 화염을 간직한 왕중왕(王中王)이자, 한 자루의 활로 숱한 전장을 지배한 천하 무림의 별이며, 살아 있는 무림의 전설들이다.
127|
128|또한.
129|
130|저벅.
131|
132|나 역시 그들과 함께할 자격을 얻었다.
133|
134|지금 이 순간 화왕과 궁성을 향해 걸어갈 수 있는 하나의 상징이 되었다.
135|
136|비록 그들보다 조금 작고, 아직은 보다 나약할지언정.
137|
138|나는, 열화신룡(烈火神龍) 진태경은 이 엿 같은 전쟁 속에서 일어난 또 한 명의 거인이었다.
139|
140|구구구구궁!
141|
142|땅이 떨린다. 아니, 몸부림친다.
143|
144|등 뒤의 야트막한 언덕 하나를 제외하면 사방이 탁 트여 있던 이 갈대숲은, 어느덧 자욱한 먼지구름에 둘러싸여 있었다.
145|
146|아니, 어디에서 왔는지 무엇인지도 모르는 괴물들에게 포위되어 있다.
147|
148|하지만.
149|
150|“아직도 저런 잡것들한테 겁먹은 놈들이 있나?”
151|
152|나는 놈들이 두렵지 않다.
153|
154|두려운 것이 있다면 오직, 내 잘못으로 인해 죽음을 맞이할 누군가의 불행뿐이다.
155|
156|“만약 두렵다면, 피하고 싶다면 지금이라도 전열에서 물러나라. 결코 비난하지 않을 테니.”
157|
158|내 모든 말들은 진심이었다.
159|
160|누구에게나 가족이, 지켜야 할 것이 있다.
161|
162|생존에 있어 비겁함이란 없다.
163|
164|그렇게라도 살아서 돌아가고자 하는 이가 있다면, 나는 그를 기꺼이 보호할 것이다.
165|
166|몇 년 전, 어둡고 악취 나던 그 동굴에서 누군가가 나를 위해 그러했듯이.
167|
168|그리고 지금 내 곁에는, 목숨을 걸고 지킬 가치가 있는 이들이 있었다.
169|
170|“씨바 거, 인생 뭐 있습니까? 조장님 뒤꽁무니만 쫓다 보니까 이제는 천마 할애비가 나타나도 안 쫄립니다.”
171|
172|혁무진이 불쑥 내뱉은 한마디에 곳곳에서 실소가 터져 나온 그때, 녀석이 나직이 덧붙였다.
173|
174|“따르겠습니다. 지옥 끝까지라도.”
175|
176|“……!”
177|
178|“……!”
179|
180|일순간, 주위의 공기가 찌르르 울렸다.
181|
182|지금 이 순간만큼은 사방을 뒤덮은 거대한 울림들도, 그 너머에서 울려 퍼지는 괴물들의 괴성도 이 세상에서 지워진 듯했다.
183|
184|동시에, 그 모든 것을 몰아내는 강철의 파도가 일어났다.
185|
186|차차차차창!
187|
188|모두가 손에 쥔 병장기를 곧추세우며 함성을 내질렀다.
189|
190|육신의 피로도, 본 적 없는 괴물들에 의한 공포도 잊은 그들은 맹수처럼 포효하며 일렁이는 어둠 속을 노려보았다.
191|
192|자신들이 이곳에 있어야 하는 이유를 떠올리며, 놈들에 의해 죽어 간 그리운 얼굴들을 떠올리며.
193|
194|그리고 그런 그들의 선두에는, 바로 내가 있다.
195|
196|“오직 두 가지만 명심해라.”
197|
198|나는 선봉을 향해 걸음을 옮기며 말을 이었다.
199|
200|“첫째. 어떤 상황에서도 현재의 진형을 유지할 것.”
201|
202|처처척!
203|
204|나아가는 걸음을 따라 갈라지는 인(人)의 파도.
205|
206|더불어 그 너머로 모습을 드러내는 빈자리.
207|
208|각각 일천의 병력이 결집한 다른 곳과 달리, 텅 비어 있는 그곳은 당장이라도 허물어트릴 수 있는 거대한 구멍처럼 보였지만 이제는 아니었다.
209|
210|“둘째.”
211|
212|사박.
213|
214|갈대를 밟으며 제자리에 멈춰 섰다.
215|
216|좌측에는 궁성이, 우측에는 적천강이.
217|
218|그리고 우리 세 사람의 등 뒤에는, 당연하다는 듯이 나를 따라온 화룡각의 대원들이.
219|
220|머릿수로 치자면 한 줌도 되지 않지만, 그것만으로도 비어 있던 선두의 공간이 빈틈없이 메워지며 하나의 진이 완성되었다.
221|
222|“어떻게 해서라도, 반드시 살아남을 것.”
223|
224|마지막 한 마디를 내뱉은 그때.
225|
226|그그그긍!
227|
228|하늘이 갈라지는 듯한 굉음과 함께, 무수한 그림자들이 온 사방을 뒤덮으며 쏟아졌다.
229|
230|삼천여 명의 정예로 이루어진 원형진(元型陳)을 향해.
231|
232|아니, 강철로 무장한 이 거대한 수레바퀴를 향해.
233|
234|쉬이이잉, 콰앙!
235|
236|궁성의 손가락 끝을 떠난 빛줄기가 어둠을 찢어발기며 폭발한 그 순간.
237|
238|콰드드득!
239|
240|강철의, 죽음의 수레바퀴가 마침내 이 세상의 것이 아닌 괴물들과 맞닿았다.
241|
242|딸랑.
243|
244|음산하고도 사이한 방울 소리가, 휘몰아치는 피 보라 너머로 울려 퍼지고 있었다.
245|
246|
247|
248|* * *
249|
250|
251|
252|그들은 짙은 어둠 속에 존재하고 있었다.
253|
254|아니, 어쩌면 적어도 지금 이 순간만큼은 그들이 어둠 그 자체일지도 몰랐다.
255|
256|그들은 단순히 어둠 속에 숨어 있는 것이 아닌, 어둠을 장막으로 삼아 몸을 가리고 있었으니까.
257|
258|설령 한 사람 한 사람이 흑의(黑衣)로 전신을 빈틈없이 둘러싸지 않았더라도, 그들을 둘러싼 장막을 간파해 내고 안을 엿볼 수 있는 이는 극히 드물었다.
259|
260|그리고 그런 위협을 줄 수 있는 이들은, 수백여 장이나 떨어진 곳에서 무수한 괴물들과 맞서 싸우는 와중이었다.
261|
262|정확히는, 그들의 조종에 따라 움직이는 수하들이었지만.
263|
264|딸랑.
265|
266|흑의인은 손에 쥔 요령(妖鈴)을 흔들었다.
267|
268|낡고 거무튀튀한 그것으로부터 흘러나온 방울 소리는 탁했으나, 한편으로는 선명하게 뻗어 나가 또 다른 명령과 정보를 전달하고 있었다.
269|
270|사방에 일정한 거리를 두고 숨어 있는, 흑의인의 또 다른 동료들이 그러하듯이.
271|
272|“마침내 시작됐군.”
273|
274|콰아앙!
275|
276|저 멀리, 굉음과 함께 번뜩이는 섬광을 확인한 흑의인은 작게 중얼거렸다.
277|
278|괴물들이 쉴 새 없이 내지르는 괴성으로 인해 소리만으로는 정확한 판단이 불가능했지만, 궁성의 것임이 분명한 저 빛줄기는 전투가 시작되었다는 증거였다.
279|
280|“목표로 했던 위치는 아니지만…… 그래도 포위망은 제대로 갖추었으니 그나마 다행인가.”
281|
282|흑의인은 못내 아쉬웠다.
283|
284|일각.
285|
286|단 일각만 더 놈들이 빠르게 움직여 갈대숲을 빠져나갔다면, 자신과 동료들은 훨씬 더 유리한 위치를 점한 채 전투를 시작할 수 있었을 것이다.
287|

*Step.*

[P94]
I stopped among the reeds.

[P95]
Bow Saint stood to my left, Jeok Cheongang to my right. Behind the three of us stood the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion, who’d followed me as though it were the most natural thing in the world.

[P96]
There were only a handful of us, but we filled the gap at the front. The formation was complete.

[P97]
“Survive. Whatever it takes.”

[P98]
The instant I spoke those final words—

[P99]
*Rrrrrumble!*

[P100]
A deafening roar sounded as if the sky had split open, and countless shadows poured in from every direction.

[P101]
Toward the circular formation of some three thousand elite fighters.

[P102]
No. Toward an enormous wheel armed in steel.

[P103]
*Whoooosh—BOOM!*

[P104]
A streak of light flew from Bow Saint’s fingertips, tore through the darkness, and exploded.

[P105]
*Craaaack!*

[P106]
The steel wheel—the wheel of death—met the monsters that did not belong in this world.

[P107]
*Jingle.*

[P108]
Beyond the swirling spray of blood, the eerie, sinister ringing of a bell carried through the air.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
They were there in the deep darkness.

[P111]
No. At least for now, perhaps they *were* the darkness.

[P112]
They weren’t merely hiding in it. They wore it like a curtain, concealing their bodies behind it. Even if they hadn’t been covered head to toe in black, precious few people could have seen through that curtain.

[P113]
And those who posed any such threat were hundreds of yards away, fighting countless monsters.

[P114]
Monsters that, to be precise, were moving under the black-clad figures’ control.

[P115]
*Jingle.*

[P116]
One of the figures shook the sinister bell in his hand.

[P117]
The sound from the old, blackened bell was dull, yet it carried clearly into the distance, conveying another set of orders and information. His comrades, hidden at regular intervals on every side, were doing the same.

[P118]
“So it’s finally begun.”

[P119]
*BOOM!*

[P120]
A flash lit up the distance with a tremendous boom, and the man muttered to himself.

[P121]
The monsters’ ceaseless roars made it impossible to tell much from sound alone. But that streak of light was unmistakably Bow Saint’s. The battle had begun.

[P122]
“It’s not where we wanted them… Still, at least we managed to surround them.”

[P123]
He couldn’t help feeling disappointed.

[P124]
Fifteen minutes. If the enemy had moved just fifteen minutes faster and cleared the reed bed, he and his comrades could have begun the battle from a far more advantageous position.

[P125]
“But it’s started now. Nothing to be done.”

[P126]
The battle was underway, and the task assigned to the thirty sorcerers, himself included, was clear.

[P127]
“Reduce their numbers as much as possible. If you can, capture Jin Taekyung alive.”

[P128]
He quietly repeated the order the Blood Lord had sent half a day earlier and frowned.

[P129]
“Capture him alive? Not kill him?”

[P130]
He’d received information on the enemy before the order arrived. It was absurd.

[P131]
Their force included no fewer than six Supreme Peak masters. Two of them were the Fire King and Bow Saint.

[P132]
If the sorcerers threw everything they had at Jin Taekyung alone, they might well kill him. Capturing him alive was another matter entirely.

[P133]
“Damn it.”

[P134]
The curse at the Blood Lord slipped out before he could stop it. He sucked in a breath and glanced around.

[P135]
But, as always, there were only monsters standing vacantly nearby, reeking horribly.

[P136]
“…Fuck this.”

[P137]
He glared at his subordinates. He hated the sight of himself trembling at the thought of the Blood Lord, who was far away. Today, the mindless monsters that did nothing but stink seemed especially loathsome too.

[P138]
“Stupid things.”

[P139]
*Jingle.*

[P140]
He shook the bell as if shooing away flies. The hundred monsters gathered around him as guards immediately began to back away.

[P141]
Or so he understood they were supposed to.

[P142]
*Step.*

[P143]
“…?”

[P144]
He blinked.

[P145]
Ninety-nine monsters had backed away. The remaining one had taken a step forward.

[P146]
“What in the—”

[P147]
Before he could find the words, the monster seemed to realize what it had done. Its backside twitched as it floundered for a moment, then it spoke.

[P148]
“W-Wow. Amazing. Never seen a monster like this before, have you?”

[P149]
“…!”

[P150]
“I-I haven’t either. Ah, shit.”

[P151]
The trembling monster—or rather, the person it clearly was—made a miserable face and sighed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

No—not dust clouds. Monsters we knew nothing about, from places we couldn’t name.

[P63]
But—

[P64]
“Anyone still scared of those worthless bastards?”

[P65]
I wasn’t afraid of them.

[P66]
The only thing I feared was someone dying because I’d made a mistake.

[P67]
“If you’re afraid—if you want to get away—leave the formation now. I won’t blame you.”

[P68]
I meant it.

[P69]
Everyone had family, something they had to protect. There was no cowardice in trying to survive.

[P70]
If anyone needed to fall back to make it home alive, I would gladly protect them.

[P71]
Just as someone had protected me years ago in that dark, reeking cave.

[P72]
And now, beside me, were people worth risking my life to protect.

[P73]
“Fuck it, what’s life anyway? I’ve spent so long chasing after you, Captain, I wouldn’t even flinch if the Heavenly Demon’s granddad showed up.”

[P74]
Hyuk Mujin’s outburst drew quiet laughter from around us. Then he added, his voice low:

[P75]
“I’ll follow you. Even to the ends of hell.”

[P76]
“…!”

[P77]
“…!”

[P78]
For an instant, the air seemed to hum.

[P79]
The tremendous rumbling around us and the monsters’ roars beyond it might as well have vanished. In their place rose a wave of steel.

[P80]
*Clang, clang, clang, clang!*

[P81]
Weapons lifted, and a shout went up.

[P82]
The fighters forgot their exhaustion and their fear of monsters they’d never seen. They roared like beasts, glaring into the shifting darkness.

[P83]
They remembered why they had to be here. They remembered the faces of those they missed, the people the monsters had killed.

[P84]
And at their head stood me.

[P85]
“Remember two things.”

[P86]
I walked toward the vanguard as I spoke.

[P87]
“First. Keep the formation, no matter what happens.”

[P88]
*Clack, clack, clack!*

[P89]
A tide of people parted before me, revealing the empty space beyond.

[P90]
A thousand fighters had gathered in each of the other sections. By comparison, this gap looked like a massive hole the enemy could break through at any moment.

[P91]
It wasn’t one anymore.

[P92]
“Second.”

[P93]
*Step.*

[P94]
I stopped among the reeds.

[P95]
Bow Saint stood to my left, Jeok Cheongang to my right. Behind the three of us stood the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion, who’d followed me as though it were the most natural thing in the world.

[P96]
There were only a handful of us, but we filled the gap at the front. The formation was complete.

[P97]
“Survive. Whatever it takes.”

[P98]
The instant I spoke those final words—

[P99]
*Rrrrrumble!*

[P100]
A deafening roar sounded as if the sky had split open, and countless shadows poured in from every direction.

[P101]
Toward the circular formation of some three thousand elite fighters.

[P102]
No. Toward an enormous wheel armed in steel.

[P103]
*Whoooosh—BOOM!*

[P104]
A streak of light flew from Bow Saint’s fingertips, tore through the darkness, and exploded.

[P105]
*Craaaack!*

[P106]
The steel wheel—the wheel of death—met the monsters that did not belong in this world.

[P107]
*Jingle.*

[P108]
Beyond the swirling spray of blood, the eerie, sinister ringing of a bell carried through the air.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
They were there in the deep darkness.

[P111]
No. At least for now, perhaps they *were* the darkness.

[P112]
They weren’t merely hiding in it. They wore it like a curtain, concealing their bodies behind it. Even if they hadn’t been covered head to toe in black, precious few people could have seen through that curtain.

[P113]
And those who posed any such threat were hundreds of yards away, fighting countless monsters.

[P114]
Monsters that, to be precise, were moving under the black-clad figures’ control.

[P115]
*Jingle.*

[P116]
One of the figures shook the sinister bell in his hand.

[P117]
The sound from the old, blackened bell was dull, yet it carried clearly into the distance, conveying another set of orders and information. His comrades, hidden at regular intervals on every side, were doing the same.

[P118]
“So it’s finally begun.”

[P119]
*BOOM!*

[P120]
A flash lit up the distance with a tremendous boom, and the man muttered to himself.

[P121]
The monsters’ ceaseless roars made it impossible to tell much from sound alone. But that streak of light was unmistakably Bow Saint’s. The battle had begun.

[P122]
“It’s not where we wanted them… Still, at least we managed to surround them.”

[P123]
He couldn’t help feeling disappointed.

[P124]
Fifteen minutes. If the enemy had moved just fifteen minutes faster and cleared the reed bed, he and his comrades could have begun the battle from a far more advantageous position.

[P125]
“But it’s started now. Nothing to be done.”

[P126]
The battle was underway, and the task assigned to the thirty sorcerers, himself included, was clear.

[P127]
“Reduce their numbers as much as possible. If you can, capture Jin Taekyung alive.”

[P128]
He quietly repeated the order the Blood Lord had sent half a day earlier and frowned.

[P129]
“Capture him alive? Not kill him?”

[P130]
He’d received information on the enemy before the order arrived. It was absurd.

[P131]
Their force included no fewer than six Supreme Peak masters. Two of them were the Fire King and Bow Saint.

[P132]
If the sorcerers threw everything they had at Jin Taekyung alone, they might well kill him. Capturing him alive was another matter entirely.

[P133]
“Damn it.”

[P134]
The curse at the Blood Lord slipped out before he could stop it. He sucked in a breath and glanced around.

[P135]
But, as always, there were only monsters standing vacantly nearby, reeking horribly.

[P136]
“…Fuck this.”

[P137]
He glared at his subordinates. He hated the sight of himself trembling at the thought of the Blood Lord, who was far away. Today, the mindless monsters that did nothing but stink seemed especially loathsome too.

[P138]
“Stupid things.”

[P139]
*Jingle.*

[P140]
He shook the bell as if shooing away flies. The hundred monsters gathered around him as guards immediately began to back away.

[P141]
Or so he understood they were supposed to.

[P142]
*Step.*

[P143]
“…?”

[P144]
He blinked.

[P145]
Ninety-nine monsters had backed away. The remaining one had taken a step forward.

[P146]
“What in the—”

[P147]
Before he could find the words, the monster seemed to realize what it had done. Its backside twitched as it floundered for a moment, then it spoke.

[P148]
“W-Wow. Amazing. Never seen a monster like this before, have you?”

[P149]
“…!”

[P150]
“I-I haven’t either. Ah, shit.”

[P151]
The trembling monster—or rather, the person it clearly was—made a miserable face and sighed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
